title: Tiered trial credits experiment: adaptive expiry + upgrade nudges
creator: Leah Park
description: Run a multi-variant experiment to optimize free-trial credit size, expiry behavior, and upgrade nudges for both self-serve orgs and trial-request enterprises. The goal is to improve PLG conversion (trial -> paid) while limiting token abuse and ensuring enterprise security/contract flows are respected. This ticket coordinates PM, design, engineering, legal, and security questionnaire updates needed for the experiment rollout.
hypothesis: H1: Increasing initial credits for new self-serve orgs from 100k tokens to 250k tokens will increase 14-day activation and 30-day paid conversion by at least 12% for developer-first apps.

H2: Adaptive expiry (credits expire 60 days by default but extended to 180 days if org completes security questionnaire / verifies billing) will reduce churn and show higher retention without materially increasing cost to Redwood.
H3: Contextual upgrade nudges (in-app banner + targeted email after 50% credit usage or at plateaued engagement) will increase upgrade rate relative to passive billing CTA by 18%.
Risk: Larger credits may be abused by automated scraping/low-value workloads — mitigation via rate limits, usage caps, and fraud detection rules is required.
experiment_design: Cohort A (Control): 100k credits, 60-day expiry, standard upgrade CTA in billing page.
Cohort B (Credit hike): 250k credits, 60-day expiry, same CTA as control.
Cohort C (Adaptive expiry): 250k credits, 60-day expiry by default; expiry extended to 180 days if org completes security questionnaire and verifies billing details; includes early upgrade nudges.

Cohort D (Enterprise-path): For orgs that self-identify as enterprise or request a trial, issue 500k credits with manual account review; skip automatic nudges and route to AE workflow and contract/SQ queue.

Randomization: New signups (first org member) will be randomized at signup. Exclude internal Redwood test orgs and flagged CI/test emails. Sample size target: 3,000 orgs total across cohorts over 30 days.

Nudges: In-app modal at 50% usage, banner on console at 75%, and an automated email sequence (Day 7 after signup, Day 20, Day 45) tailored by cohort. Messages will highlight unit cost, saving on reserved capacity, and an easy upgrade flow.

Abuse mitigation: Per-org soft rate limit of 60 requests/min by default for trial cohorts, automatic anomaly detection to flag unusually high throughput, and temporary throttling before credits are exhausted.
Data collection: Track activation events (first successful generation), average tokens/day, time-to-first-upgrade, N-day retention, conversion funnel, and support/AE touchpoints.
Segmentation: Track results by org size, vertical (if provided), region, and initial usage pattern (embedding-heavy vs. text-gen-heavy).
rollout_plan: Week 1: Engineering feature flag + backend support for variant issuance and adaptive expiry; basic monitoring dashboards deployed.
Week 2: Design creative for in-app nudges and email templates; legal/security review of wording for SQ incentive.
Week 3: Launch to 10% of new signups for smoke test, monitor for abuse and infra impact; iterate copy and rate limits.
Week 4: Ramp to full sample if no major issues; continue monitoring; coordinate AE team for enterprise-path inflows.
Failure rollback: Revert to Control cohort credit size and expiry via feature flag; notify customers if any trial credits were overissued due to a bug.
monitoring_kpis: Primary: 30-day paid conversion rate (trial -> paid) per cohort
Activation: % of orgs issuing at least one generation within first 7 days
Engagement: median tokens/day and 7/14/30 day retention
Economics: average $ cost per converted org (estimate token cost + infra amortized)
Abuse signals: % of orgs triggering anomaly detection or manual review
Enterprise flow: time to contract or AE touchpoint for enterprise-path orgs
acceptance_criteria: Backend: Safe issuance of variant credits via feature flag and audit logs for every credit grant
UI: In-app nudges and email sequence templates implemented and A/B controllable
Metrics: Dashboard shows cohort-level KPIs and supports segmentation; daily alert on abuse thresholds
Legal/Security: Updated trial language and security questionnaire incentive approved by legal; SQ form link available in signup path for adaptive expiry extension
Runbook: Support/AE runbook for enterprise-path trial requests and credit disputes
